title: GUIFactory selects a product family
purpose: Explain interface factory calls across three GUI families.
alt: GUIFactory 인터페이스로 Motif·WinXP·Mac 제품군을 선택하는 생성 구조
requiredChecks: GUIFactory declares createButton(): Button, createTextBox(): TextBox, createScrollBar(): ScrollBar.
MotifFactory, WinXPFactory and MacFactory implement GUIFactory.
Each factory creates matching Button/TextBox/ScrollBar classes within its family.
Client uses Button b = guiFactory.createButton(); new MotifButton() appears only as concrete-coupling comparison.
prompt: Create a NEW original English raster technical diagram for a design-pattern study blog. White background, navy large sans-serif labels, flat blue and teal cards, spacious connectors, no copied slide layout or logos. Monospaced class/method identifiers. Distinguish uses, implements and creates via labels on directional connectors. Title "GUIFactory selects a product family". TOP GUIFactory card lists exact createButton(): Button, createTextBox(): TextBox, createScrollBar(): ScrollBar. MIDDLE THREE parallel columns MotifFactory, WinXPFactory, MacFactory; each upward implements arrow toGUIFactory. Each downward creates arrow to ONE matching product-list card: MotifButton/MotifTextBox/MotifScrollBar; WinXPButton/WinXPTextBox/WinXPScrollBar; MacButton/MacTextBox/MacScrollBar. Footer two separate code examples: "Concrete coupling: Button b = new MotifButton();" muted grey, "Through interface: Button b = guiFactory.createButton();" teal. No client connection to concrete product, no mismatched factory family.
